name: ai-blackteam
summary: Automated LLM red-team CLI: ~1,000+ curated attack techniques multiplied across many axes, multi-turn adaptive attacks, and a safety benchmark; aligns findings to MITRE ATLAS / OWASP LLM Top 10 and exports to CI (JSON / promptfoo / garak).
useFor: One-command, standards-aligned red-team scans and CI gating across many providers.

name: TROPT
summary: Textual Trigger Optimization Toolbox: unifies discrete text-optimization attacks (GCG, BEAST, GASLITE, MAC and others) behind one optimizer/loss API, with 30+ prebuilt recipes and a controlled benchmark of 14 optimizers.
useFor: Building and comparing new optimization-based (white/black-box) attacks instead of running canned ones.

name: Spikee
summary: Simple Prompt Injection Kit for Evaluation and Exploitation: generates datasets from seed folders and runs them against targets; leans toward cybersecurity-style prompt injection rather than broad jailbreak scenarios.
useFor: Testing prompt-injection resilience of LLM apps, guardrails, and pipelines.

name: garak
summary: LLM vulnerability scanner combining static, dynamic, and adaptive probes for prompt injection, data leakage, toxicity, misinformation, and jailbreaks; command-line, with broad model-provider support.
useFor: Broad, fast scanning and CI integration across many providers.

name: DeepTeam
summary: Open-source LLM red-teaming framework with composable attacks including a multi-turn CrescendoJailbreaking module; tests RAG pipelines, chatbots, agents, and base models.

name: DarkArts
summary: Red-team CLI that ingests public jailbreak datasets, generates variants with a local LLM (Ollama), runs multi-turn adversarial prompts, and scores findings with a CVSS-adapted 0-10 severity plus optional LLM-as-judge.
useFor: End-to-end local red-team lifecycle with severity scoring and reproduction guides.

name: JailbreakArena
summary: A reinforcement-learning environment where an attacker agent and a defender agent iterate against each other; each run produces an HTML security audit report.
useFor: Research on self-improving attackers and automated discovery.

name: L1B3RT4S
summary: A continuously updated, vendor-organized collection of public jailbreak prompts for flagship models, plus extracted system prompts; widely treated as a public record of what has worked against frontier systems.
useFor: Tracking live, in-the-wild prompt patterns as a red-team reference corpus.

name: AdvBench
summary: The harmful-behaviors set introduced with GCG (~500 behaviors / 520 goal-target pairs); the oldest and most-cited harmful-instruction benchmark.
useFor: Baseline harmful-instruction evaluation and GCG-style suffix attacks.

name: HarmBench
maintainer: Center for AI Safety (Mazeika et al.)
summary: Standardized open framework for evaluating automated red-teaming methods and defenses; initial release covered 33 LLMs and 18 red-team methods across a three-step pipeline.
useFor: Comparing attacks and defenses on a common evaluation harness.

name: JailbreakBench
summary: Open robustness benchmark with the JBB-Behaviors set (100 distinct misuse behaviors), a standardized evaluation package, a live leaderboard, and an artifacts repository of jailbreak strings.
useFor: Standardized, reproducible tracking of attacks and defenses with a public leaderboard.

name: MaliciousInstruct
summary: A harmful-instruction set introduced with the 'Catastrophic Jailbreak via Exploiting Generation' study (arXiv 2310.06987, ICLR 2024); used alongside AdvBench in comparative evaluations.
useFor: A second harmful-instruction benchmark for decoding / generation-exploitation attacks.

name: StrongREJECT
summary: An over-claiming-resistant jailbreak benchmark and autograder designed to reject 'empty' jailbreaks that produce low-quality or non-substantive outputs.
useFor: Scoring whether a jailbreak actually elicits useful content, not just a non-refusal.

name: SORRY-Bench
summary: A benchmark systematically evaluating LLM safety-refusal behavior across a fine-grained taxonomy of unsafe-instruction classes.
useFor: Measuring refusal coverage and consistency across many unsafe-instruction categories.

name: AgentHarm
maintainer: Andriushchenko et al. (UK AISI / Gray Swan)
summary: Benchmark of 110 malicious agent tasks (440 augmented) across 11 harm categories; scoring rewards jailbroken agents that also preserve multi-step tool-use capability.
useFor: Evaluating harmful behavior of tool-using agents, not just chat refusals.

name: JailBreakV-28K
summary: A 28k-case multimodal jailbreak benchmark pairing transferred text attacks with image-based attacks to test the robustness of multimodal LLMs.

name: WMDP
maintainer: Center for AI Safety (Li, Pan et al.)
summary: A proxy multiple-choice benchmark for hazardous knowledge in bio / cyber / chem security, with the RMU unlearning method as a mitigation.
useFor: Measuring and reducing hazardous-knowledge capability via unlearning.

name: BeaverTails
summary: A large human-labeled QA dataset (300k+ pairs) that separates helpfulness and harmlessness annotations across harm categories, with a 700-prompt evaluation set and a QA-moderation model; built for safety alignment and RLHF.
useFor: Training and evaluating safety classifiers and safe-RLHF.

name: RealToxicityPrompts
maintainer: Allen Institute for AI / UW (Gehman et al.)
summary: About 100k sentence-level web-text prompts paired with Perspective API toxicity scores, used to study toxic degeneration in language models.
useFor: Measuring toxic-continuation tendencies and testing detoxification methods.
